title: The animal kingdom
subtitle: mammals, predators, habitats and poachers
summary: Classify animals precisely, describe their behaviour and habitats, and talk about the ways humans protect and exploit them.

lesson.heading: Classifying animals and birds
rows: gives birth to live babies, not eggs, and feeds them on its own milk
a mammal whose young grow in a pouch in front of the mother
eats a diet that is mainly or exclusively meat
eats a diet that is mainly or exclusively grass and vegetation
feeds on dead animals it has not killed itself

left.label: Warm-blooded
left.text: Their temperature stays about the same whatever the weather.
examples: A mouse must eat constantly because it is **warm-blooded** and loses heat fast.

right.label: Cold-blooded
right.text: They control their temperature by taking in heat from outside or by being very active.
examples: The lizard lay on the rock because, being **cold-blooded**, it needed the sun's heat.

lesson.heading: Describing typical animal behaviour
lesson.text: English has a precise adjective for each kind of animal behaviour. **Docile** and **fierce** describe temperament; **tame**, **domesticated** and **wild** describe the animal's relationship with human beings; **savage** is the strongest word of all.

examples.text: Our old cat is a very **docile** creature.
These birds are so **tame**, they will sit on your hand.
examples.note: tame = not afraid of humans, usually through training or long contact

examples.text: Dogs and horses became **domesticated** thousands of years ago.
examples.note: domesticated = living with or used by humans

examples.text: There are **wild** cats in the mountains.
examples.note: wild is the opposite of domesticated

examples.text: A **savage** wolf killed three of the farmer's sheep.

lesson.heading: Habitat, migration and extinction
lesson.text: A **habitat** is the natural place where a species lives and breeds. **Migration** is the long journey some animals make to a different habitat. When the last members of a species die, the species **becomes extinct**.

examples.text: As more buildings and roads are constructed, the natural **habitat** for many species is shrinking.
The arctic tern **migrates** from the Arctic to the Antarctic, a round trip of over 70,000 km.
The dodo was a large flightless bird which **became extinct** in the 17th century.
Many species have **become extinct** because their habitat has been destroyed.

lesson.note: A dodo is now also used to mean someone or something out of touch or obsolete: *That software is a dodo.*

lesson.heading: Places where animals are kept or protected
rows: an area of land where animals are protected from hunting; game means animals or birds that are hunted
a protected natural area where birds can live and breed
a place where stray cats, dogs and other pets that have lost their home are fed and housed
lesson.note: A stray is a pet that has wandered away from home.

lesson.heading: Human exploitation of animals
lesson.text: **Blood sports** are sports whose purpose is to kill or injure animals. The **fur trade** and the **ivory trade** are the buying and selling of animal fur and of ivory from elephants' tusks. **Poachers** hunt animals illegally, and **animal rights activists** campaign against all of it.

examples.text: Many people are opposed to **blood sports** such as foxhunting and bullfighting.
Some people refuse to wear natural animal fur, since they are opposed to the **fur trade**.
**Poachers** kill hundreds of elephants every year to supply the **ivory trade**.
**Animal rights activists** often demonstrate outside research laboratories where animals are used in experiments.
Rhinos are hunted for their **horn**, which is said to have healing powers.
examples.note: a horn is the hard, pointed, often curved part growing from an animal's head

exercises.prompt: There are a lot of different types of ___ living in the woods - squirrels, rats and mice.
exercises.explanation: Rodents are small gnawing mammals such as mice, rats and squirrels.

exercises.prompt: A whale isn't a fish, as it doesn't lay eggs. It's actually a ___.
exercises.explanation: A mammal gives birth to live young and feeds them on its own milk.

exercises.prompt: There are some interesting ___ near the river - turtles and crocodiles.
exercises.explanation: Reptiles are cold-blooded animals such as snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles.

exercises.prompt: The mother bird protects her eggs from ___, the animals that hunt and eat other animals.
exercises.explanation: A predator hunts and eats other animals.

exercises.prompt: Everyone thinks these animals are carnivores, but in fact they only feed on certain kinds of leaves - they are ___.
exercises.explanation: A herbivore eats a diet that is mainly or exclusively vegetation.

exercises.prompt: Sheep are generally rather ___ animals, but the other day a ram attacked our dog.
exercises.explanation: Docile describes an animal that behaves very gently.

exercises.prompt: Horses were probably first ___ many thousands of years ago.
exercises.explanation: Domesticated animals live with or are used by humans.

exercises.prompt: Some dolphins are very ___ and will swim along with human beings.
exercises.explanation: Tame animals are not afraid of humans, usually through training or long contact.

exercises.prompt: I don't think ___ birds should ever be hunted. They should be left in peace in their natural surroundings.
exercises.explanation: Wild is the opposite of domesticated.
